comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C14-C20. Both evaluations support that mice failed to learn spatial location when entrance positions were randomized. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis while peer reviewers accept these findings as valid controls without challenge.

Strong agreement on spatial learning with static entrances (C21-C29). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation while peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as the core finding. Peer result R1 also includes C1 and C7 (main conclusions) which OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Agreement on TEV computational framework and differential learning dynamics (C2, C3, C30). OpenEval explicitly validates the TEV analysis while peer reviewers implicitly accept it without raising concerns about the analytical approach.

Perfect agreement on claims C8, C32, C33. Both evaluations strongly support that mice use idiothetic rather than allothetic cues, with rotation experiments demonstrating REL behavior. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight this as a key strength.

Agreement on claims C34-C36 regarding visual cue independence. OpenEval notes minor limitation about odor controls while peer reviewers accept findings without challenge. Peer result also includes C81 not mentioned in OpenEval result.

Strong agreement on shortcut behavior (C4, C9, C38-C40). Both evaluations affirm this as meeting Tolman's criteria for cognitive maps. OpenEval notes behavioral variability (5/8 mice) while peer reviewers describe experiments as 'conclusive.' Peer result also includes C41-C42 which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Agreement on path integration basis of cognitive map (C41-C42). OpenEval provides detailed validation of rotation control experiments while peer reviewers include these claims within broader shortcut discussion (R3 covers C4, C9, C38-C42).

Agreement on central finding (C1, C7) that mice can form cognitive maps using path integration. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of multiple experimental results while peer reviewers provide explicit affirmation from all reviewers. Peer result R1 primarily focuses on C21-C29 but includes these main conclusions.

Agreement on apparatus design (C10-C12, C104-C105). OpenEval validates methodological descriptions while peer reviewers praise the novel HFM design and rotationally symmetric features. Peer result R10 covers broader methodological claims including subject details and procedures.

Agreement on claim C13 regarding thigmotaxis. OpenEval validates this behavioral observation while peer reviewers do not specifically address it but accept overall experimental design without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C37, C97-C98. Both evaluations support that shortcuts were not learned through incidental exposure. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis while peer reviewers accept these controls as part of thoughtfully designed experiments.

Agreement on hole checking behavior analysis (C76, C94-C96). OpenEval validates detailed temporal and entropy analyses while peer reviewers explicitly highlight active sensing and uncertainty reduction as strengths. Peer result also includes C31 which OpenEval addresses in R3.

Agreement on trajectory segment analysis (C90-C91). OpenEval validates heading angle analysis while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through acknowledgment of active sensing role. Peer result also includes C76 which OpenEval addresses in R12.

Agreement on experimental subjects and ethical approval (C101-C103). OpenEval notes lack of statistical analysis for sex differences while peer reviewers accept these routine methodological details without concern.

Agreement on experimental conditions and data collection (C106-C111). OpenEval validates standard methodological details while peer reviewers accept these without raising concerns. Both evaluations find methods adequately documented.

Agreement on neural mechanism speculation (C43-C44). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of direct testing while peer reviewers praise the theoretical discussion. Both accept these as reasonable hypotheses appropriately qualified by authors.

Agreement on literature review and theoretical framework (C5-C6, C45-C89). OpenEval validates citations and literature representation while peer reviewers explicitly praise the rich discussion. Both evaluations accept the positioning within existing literature.

Partial overlap on background literature (C5, C6, C51-C56). OpenEval groups all literature citations together while peer reviewers separately address these foundational claims. Both accept these as accurate representations of prior work.

Agreement on hypothesis about start location importance (C87). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting speculative nature while peer reviewers accept within broader theoretical discussion. Both recognize this as hypothesis for future investigation rather than directly tested claim.
